descriptions.auth.enterprise-sso: Users authenticate through the customer's identity provider — OIDC providers brokered via the platform Keycloak, SAML federations with metadata, SP-initiated login, ACS, and single logout, and edge-terminated client-certificate (CAC/PKI smartcard) login — with platform-managed sessions, token refresh, and logout, so access is enterprise identity end to end. The analyst-side login steps and the admin-side wiring steps converge on the same mechanism from both ends.
descriptions.authz.rebac-access-control: Access to platform resources is decided by relationship tuples, subject and group administration, and attribute gates: administrators manage tuples and subjects, applications ask check-access questions and receive decisions with recorded reasons, datasets carry attribute-gate bindings evaluated per caller, and every decision is logged — the policy layer the security docs ship as ReBAC, deny-by-default over an explicit subject → relation → object model.
descriptions.catalog.registered-sources: Register S3 and PostgreSQL sources, then scan into the governed catalog.
descriptions.catalog.writable-datasets: Manage file content inside platform-managed datasets.
descriptions.connectors.ai-assisted-connector-setup: Use a selected model to propose or attempt connector setup and bounded repair, with live preview and revision checks.
descriptions.connectors.connector-builder: Import OpenAPI, Postman, documentation or PDF text into a connector project; test its definition, generate a tool package and deploy a dedicated connector runtime.
descriptions.connectors.oauth-tool-policies: An app owner or administrator sets, for one app installation, tool and provider, the list of provider operations the tool may call through the OAuth broker, such as gmail.search without gmail.send. On the broker's standard proxy path, a call whose operation is not on that list is refused.
descriptions.context.dataset-indexing: Bind a catalog dataset to a searchable semantic/lexical index.
descriptions.context.workroom-ingestion-summary: A workroom member who can view the workroom reads one summary of what has been ingested into it: how many data sources it has, broken down by source type, when the earliest and latest sources were created, the total error count across those sources, and how many catalog datasets are tagged to the workroom.
descriptions.context.workroom-raw-file-store: Store, list, read and update workroom raw files.
descriptions.delegation.pending-approval-queue: An approver lists the delegated-workload effects in their tenant that are waiting for a human decision, polls that list from the SDK, and approves or denies an effect from it. The queue is an API and SDK surface; no approval inbox ships in the UI.
descriptions.federation.federated-retrieval: The sovereignty question in a multi-site deployment is whether analysis requires moving data. Here it does not: an analyst discovers datasets on a paired cluster and runs retrieval there, the remote cluster's own catalog and retrieval services process the request against its own adapters, and only the results come back. The data stays where its owner keeps it.
descriptions.ingestion.document-translation: Translate parsed Markdown into a requested language through a configured model and retrieve persisted language artifacts.
descriptions.ingestion.parse-from-url: OmniParse downloads a document from a public HTTP or HTTPS URL on the server and stores it as a document record. The caller then reads the record as Markdown or HTML, or reads its chunks, tables or figures, through the same document routes used for uploaded files. Tables, figures and chunks are declared in ingestion.structured-document-outputs.
descriptions.ingestion.scheduled-ingest: Ingestion runs on demand: a registered source type is ingested immediately through one call, a DDE connector's ingest is triggered per connector, and the results land as catalog datasets owned by the requester. A job-registration API with cron syntax and pollable status exists alongside — but read the not_supported entry before claiming schedules: at the pinned revision registered jobs are stored, not executed.
descriptions.ingestion.structured-document-outputs: Expose structured tables, figure metadata and text chunks from supported parsed documents.
descriptions.ingestion.video-frame-analysis: Upload a video to OmniParse as an asynchronous job. The job pulls keyframes and the audio track out of the video, asks a vision model to describe each keyframe, transcribes the audio, and stores the keyframe images, descriptions and transcript for retrieval.
descriptions.kaizen.admin-settings-console: Inspect effective configuration and change/reset audited settings.
descriptions.kaizen.agent-auto-routing: Kaizen can bring one specialist agent into a chat turn to help the agent serving it, picked on the server from the agents that serving agent may call. Each member can pin the agent that serves their chats, allow specialist help for it, and leave agents out of that pinned agent's specialist help. Specialist help is a consult: the serving agent keeps the turn and the answer.
descriptions.kaizen.agent-publication-approval: Members submit agent and package proposals; a Kaizen administrator approves or rejects them, and can later disable, re-enable or roll back an agent.
descriptions.kaizen.answer-feedback: Members give a thumbs up or thumbs down on a chat answer. Kaizen records the vote as an audit event that administrator metrics count.
descriptions.kaizen.artifacts: Create and revise agent outputs; inspect versions, fork and share permitted artifacts.
descriptions.kaizen.context-compression: Members can opt in to compressing code-execution output, a terse Plain-speak answer style and prompt trim, see estimated savings, and compact a long conversation.
descriptions.kaizen.conversation-event-streaming: An integration opens a Kaizen conversation's live event stream (server-sent events) instead of polling, replays events after a journal position, and can send a message and wait for the agent's reply over that stream. This is the primary Kaizen 0.7.1 conversation contract, reached through the platform SDK.
descriptions.kaizen.conversation-search: Search authorized conversations and navigate document/project results in primary Kaizen.
descriptions.kaizen.document-canvas-export: A member opens one of their own uploaded documents in an editable canvas, and can export the current text as Markdown, Word (DOCX) or PDF through the API; the web app has no export control at this revision. Edits made in the canvas are saved as new versions through the artifact revision route, which kaizen.artifacts declares.
descriptions.kaizen.document-collections: Maintain named document collections for primary Kaizen library and grounding workflows.
descriptions.kaizen.member-token-budget: When an operator sets a positive daily cap, Kaizen refuses a member's direct model calls for the rest of the UTC day once that member's recorded token use reaches it. No cap is set by default.
descriptions.kaizen.metrics-dashboard: Read primary Kaizen administrator metrics, usage snapshots and separately audited member-usage summaries.
descriptions.kaizen.multi-agent-orchestration: Coordinate specialist child work with bounded plans and durable traces.
descriptions.kaizen.notifications-inbox: List member notifications and mark one/all read.
descriptions.kaizen.platform-operator-tools: Closed SDK tools inspect platform resources and preview/apply bounded Demo Blueprint actions.
descriptions.kaizen.prebuilt-agents: Kaizen ships four ready-made agents (Web Researcher, Software Engineer, Ontology Builder and Demo Builder), provisions them at startup, and publishes them to every member.
descriptions.kaizen.privacy-guard: Kaizen Legacy's Privacy Guard checks a chat message in the browser before it is sent. In warn mode it shows the user the likely emails, phone numbers, Social Security numbers, IPv4 addresses and secrets it found and lets them choose what to send. In redact mode it replaces each one with <REDACTED> and sends the result.
descriptions.kaizen.product-identity: Kaizen v3 and Kaizen v4 are separate products that share catalog names. This decides which product a given release is, and whether a claimant on a reserved Kaizen name is the genuine article.
descriptions.kaizen.projects: Group conversations and library pointers in member-authorized projects.
descriptions.kaizen.prompt-library-and-chains: Save member prompts and validate/run versioned chains.
descriptions.kaizen.recipes: In Kaizen Legacy a user can save a tool call from search results as a named recipe that keeps the call's arguments and result. Every agent gets a recipe lookup tool that searches the saved recipes by tool name or keyword, so it can repeat a call that worked before.
descriptions.kaizen.scheduled-tasks: Preview/create owner-bound task definitions and schedule or background agent work.
descriptions.kaizen.shared-chat-typing-indicators: In a Kaizen chat shared with other members, each participant sees which other members are present and which of them are typing.
descriptions.kaizen.workroom-notes: In Kaizen Legacy, analysts can create Markdown notes in a workroom and edit notes and other text files in a side-pane editor, and the chat agent can create notes with its create_note tool. Notes are files named kaizen-notes/<slug>.md in the workroom's file list.
descriptions.models.gpu-placement: When a model is deployed on an install that has the placement operator enabled, Kamiwaza decides where it runs — which node, which GPU or memory pool, and how much memory to reserve — so that a cluster's accelerators serve more than one model deliberately rather than by accident. The platform estimates the model's VRAM footprint, classifies the hardware it could land on, reserves a budget there, and refuses fast and legibly when nothing fits. The deploy flow itself is unchanged: on such an install placement is a property of every deploy, not a separate operation.
descriptions.models.openai-compatible-inference: Applications call Kamiwaza-governed models — locally served or externally proxied — through OpenAI-compatible routes, so anything written against the OpenAI wire format runs against them without code changes. The SDK makes this concrete by handing back a standard openai.OpenAI client already pointed at a chosen deployment. This compatibility claim is distinct from deployment: it is the claim application developers actually ask about, and it can hold or fail independently of whether deploys succeed.
descriptions.models.two-node-serving: An administrator attaches a second GPU node to the head node over SSH. The serving engines can then start model containers on that node, copy downloaded model files to it, and report its GPUs in the cluster capabilities. The source describes the setup as meant for DGX Spark and similar machines.
descriptions.platform.access-requests: Request resource access and record grantor approval/denial.
descriptions.platform.airgapped-install: Classified and sovereign environments cannot reach the internet, and an installer that assumes a public registry is an installer they cannot use. At the cited revisions Kamiwaza's disconnected path is an ordinary Helm install that pulls from the customer's own registry: the release chart and the images it lists are copied into that registry by digest, and a small set of values points every image, and the App Garden catalog, inside the network.
descriptions.platform.api-reference: Serve machine-readable OpenAPI and offline interactive reference.
descriptions.platform.licensing-and-eula: Validate signed license files and surface commercial-term status.
descriptions.platform.news-feed: Display configured vendor news with offline fallback.
descriptions.platform.operations-and-notifications: Read persistent per-user operations and notification feeds.
descriptions.platform.usage-and-audit: Answering "who did what, and when" during an audit depends on the events having been recorded before anyone asked. The platform records user activity and authorization decisions, and exposes a recent-activity feed over API and SDK — the raw material an audit response is built from.
descriptions.workrooms.org-decommission: An administrator lists the organization's workrooms, creates a decommission plan with a future cutoff, and confirms it by typing the organization name. Creating the plan turns off room creation. Confirmation archives every planned room and makes rooms read-only. At the cutoff the rooms are deleted. A tombstone keeps each room's name, cutoff and retention contact.
